candidates.original_title: The neural basis of acceptance of uncertain situations: Relationship between ambiguity tolerance and the resting-state functional connectivity of the brain
candidates.description: The original study found that higher ambiguity tolerance (unidimensional) was associated with stronger connectivity within integration and control networks (IPL-MFG/MCC) and lower tolerance with stronger connectivity in threat/error-monitoring circuits (OFC-ACC). This replication tested whether three MAAS dimensions (Discomfort with Ambiguity, Absolutism, Need for Complexity) relate to resting-state functional connectivity in a Japanese sample.
candidates.citation_sentence: This preregistered study conceptually replicated and extended [9] by examining how three dimensions of the Multidimensional Attitude toward Ambiguity Scale (MAAS)-Discomfort with Ambiguity (DA), Absolutism (AB), and Need for Complexity (NC)-relate to resting-state functional connectivity in a Japanese sample.
candidates.notes: One entry for the whole study; three hypotheses tested but one conceptual replication of Liu et al. (2023). Null results for all three MAAS dimensions.

candidates.original_title: The neural basis of acceptance of uncertain situations: Relationship between ambiguity tolerance and the resting-state functional connectivity of the brain
candidates.description: Higher ambiguity tolerance was associated with stronger connectivity within integration and control networks, specifically between the inferior parietal lobule and middle frontal gyrus/middle cingulate cortex; this replication tested the corresponding association with Need for Complexity.
candidates.citation_sentence: Several methodological differences from Liu et al. (2023) may explain the divergent findings.
candidates.notes: The replication authors explicitly report that Need for Complexity was not associated with inferior parietal–middle frontal/middle cingulate connectivity and conclude that the reported ambiguity-tolerance associations were not replicated.

candidates.original_title: The neural basis of acceptance of uncertain situations: Relationship between ambiguity tolerance and the resting-state functional connectivity of the brain
candidates.description: Lower ambiguity tolerance was associated with stronger connectivity in threat- and error-monitoring circuits, operationalized in this replication as stronger amygdala–anterior insula connectivity among participants with greater Discomfort with Ambiguity.
candidates.citation_sentence: Several methodological differences from Liu et al. (2023) may explain the divergent findings.
candidates.notes: The replication authors explicitly report that Discomfort with Ambiguity was unrelated to amygdala–anterior insula connectivity and conclude that the reported ambiguity-tolerance associations were not replicated. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: The neural basis of acceptance of uncertain situations: Relationship between ambiguity tolerance and the resting-state functional connectivity of the brain
candidates.description: Lower ambiguity tolerance was associated with stronger connectivity between the orbitofrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex, reflecting threat-related warning signals; this replication tested the corresponding association with Absolutism.
candidates.citation_sentence: Several methodological differences from Liu et al. (2023) may explain the divergent findings.
candidates.notes: The replication authors explicitly report that Absolutism showed no relationship with orbitofrontal–anterior cingulate connectivity and conclude that the reported ambiguity-tolerance associations were not replicated. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
